editorial:
Imagine growing up in a world where you are just trying to play with your friends and figure out your first crush, while a massive war is happening right outside your door. You get to see this through the eyes of young Tomica in 1941 Zagreb. It starts off feeling like a sweet childhood memory, but things get wild quickly. His parents end up hiding an Italian deserter in their house, and his aunt Nadica falls head-over-heels for a German soldier. It is a strange mix of funny family moments and the scary reality of soldiers fighting in the streets. The vibe is a bit like a family scrapbook that slowly reveals some very dark secrets.

What really makes this work is how it balances the laughs with the heavy stuff. The acting feels real, and you will find yourself rooting for these messy characters even when they make bad choices. The pacing is steady, though some might find the middle a bit slow. If you enjoy stories about family ties and survival, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing how the war eventually destroys the innocent world Tomica knew. After all the romantic tension and hiding secrets, the political fighting catches up to everyone. You see the tragic cost of the conflict as the characters face the consequences of who they loved and which side they picked. It wraps up with a bittersweet feeling, leaving you to realize that childhood ends the moment the war hits home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas with a touch of humor and heart.
